2 unchanged paragraphs

!shot at-stack.webp | images/ | Four layers of the same stack. Atstack: the top,mandate, enforcement, the mandate: an Agent Behaviour Policy per role, saying what the role is granted, what it is for, the rules,record and how each rule is kept. Below it, enforcement at three levels: the prompt, hooks in the harness, and a third-party system that blocks, such as Ruflo's policy engine in enforce mode. Below that, the record: Ruflo's decision receipt for every action, and an sgit vault keeping memory and receipts encrypted and versioned. At the bottom, attestation: what was assured, signed, so that someone outside can verify it. The first three exist in ruv.sgit; the fourth is the attestation layer.attestation. | architecture

17 unchanged paragraphs, under In short {#in-short}, A summary, nearly right {#summary}, What an ABP does {#abp}…

!shot at-levels.webp | images/ | Three levels of enforcement for one rule of an Agent Behaviour Policy. Level 1,Policy: the prompt:prompt,the rule is in the agent's instructions; it sees everythinghooks and enforces nothing; the agent can ignore it; the evidence is the agent's own account. Level 2, hooks: small deterministic programs the harness runs before and after each action; they can block, but they sit on the agent's machine and are often editable by its account; the evidence is the hook's log. Level 3, a third-party system: a policy engine, gateway or service that does the blocking, out of the agent's reach; the evidence is that system's decision record. The recommended level for any rule that matters is the third.system. | comparison

7 unchanged paragraphs, under Where the receipt comes from {#receipt}, What is missing: a third party can check it {#missing}

!shot at-without-with.webp | images/ | The same question,question from a customer, an auditor or an insurer:insurer,wasansweredthis agent working under that policy,without and was each rule kept? Withoutwith an attestation layer: the operator sends the policy, the logs and the receipts; the third party cannot tell which version was in force, whether the receipts were edited, or which rules were only in the prompt; they take the operator's word. With an attestation layer: what was assured is signed, the policy version, the level of each rule, the receipts and the record's hash; the third party verifies the signature and reads what was and was not enforced; trust moves from the operator's word to a check.layer. | comparison
